claims.claim: The mere presence of a smartphone reduces available cognitive capacity even when people successfully avoid checking their phones.
claims.quote: even when people are successful at maintaining sustained attention—as when avoiding the temptation to check their phones—the mere presence of these devices reduces available cognitive capacity.

claims.claim: The cognitive costs of having a smartphone nearby are highest for people who are most dependent on their phones.
claims.quote: Moreover, these cognitive costs are highest for those highest in smartphone dependence.

claims.claim: A meta-analysis found that the mere presence of a smartphone had no significant effect on cognitive outcomes.
claims.quote: It was found that the mere presence of smartphone had no significant effect on cognitive outcomes (d = −0.02, SE = 0.02, 95% CI [−0.06, 0.01], p = .246).

claims.claim: The mere presence of a smartphone reduces basal attentional performance.
claims.quote: The results of the conducted experiment imply that the mere presence of a smartphone results in lower cognitive performance, which supports the hypothesis of the smartphone presence using limited cognitive resources.

claims.claim: Working memory capacity was negatively impacted by the mere presence of a smartphone, while other cognitive functions showed no effect.
claims.quote: Working memory capacity was negatively impacted by the mere presence of a smartphone, while results for the remaining cognitive functions produced null summary effects.

evidence.angle: The famous finding that a silent phone drains your brain is real in single experiments but shrinks to nothing when all the studies are pooled.
evidence.verdict: The evidence is mixed, with some experiments and meta-analyses showing that a smartphone's presence reduces working memory and cognitive capacity, while a larger meta-analysis found no significant overall effect.
evidence.caveat: The findings are complicated by substantial methodological heterogeneity and generally poor statistical power in the research domain.

carousel.title: The Cost of Presence

hooks.text: Does your phone drain your focus without you touching it?
You think you are ignoring your phone. The data says your brain is still processing it.
Your phone sits on the table while you try to think.
A phone sits face down on a wooden desk.

reveal.headline: The mere presence of a smartphone reduces your available cognitive capacity.
reveal.body: This happens even when you successfully avoid checking the device. [F1]

explain.headline: Your brain allocates resources to the device.
explain.body: Having a phone nearby reduces basal attentional performance [F4]. It specifically impacts your working memory capacity [F5].

matters.headline: The cost is not equal.
matters.body: The cognitive drain is highest for those most dependent on their phones. That may be why your focus feels thinner the more you rely on the screen [F2].

example.headline: A quiet dinner.
example.body: You place your phone on the table. You try to listen to the person across from you. Your brain remains partially tethered to the device in your line of sight.

question.headline: Where is your attention actually resting?
question.body: Look at where your phone is right now.

stat.label: available cognitive capacity from the mere presence of a smartphone

carousel.caption:
Your phone consumes mental energy even when it is turned off.

Research shows that the presence of a smartphone can reduce working memory and attentional performance, though some meta-analyses show no significant overall effect. Findings are complicated by poor statistical power and methodological differences.
